newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Harvey Norman eyes Asian expansion.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Harvey Norman eyes Asian expansion.

text.p: Australian retailer Harvey Norman Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it was looking at opportunities to open a furniture retailing operation in Asia.
"We can go there and do furniture tommorrow, that wouldn't be a problem," chairman Gerry Harvey told reporters after Harvey Norman's annual meeting in Sydney.
Harvey said a big opportunity for the company was to have Australian-designed furniture manufactured in Malaysia to sell to the Asian market.
"Eight years ago we sent one of our designs up to a Singapore (furniture) manufacturer that came down to see us - his best seller is still the lounge we gave him eight years ago," Harvey said.
Harvey said in terms of the Malaysian market he believed that too many shopping complexes had been built in Kuala Lumpur.
"It well may be that we get a proposition from someone because they can't fill them (shopping centres) up, then we could go over there," Harvey said.
"No one in Malaysia does furniture right, if the right proposition came along tomorrow for someone over there, we could be there the next day," he said.
Harvey said the company had visited Malaysia and stated its intentions and had discussions with a number of parties.
However, Harvey said he did not envision the company would retail computer hardware in Asia in the near future because he said piracy was rampant in Asian countries.
"At this stage of the game the way the game is played in Asia it makes it very difficult for us," he said.
Earlier, Harvey Norman director, Katie Page told the annual meeting the company's planned expansion into New Zealand was going well.
Page said the company had an agreement with its furniture manufacturer suppliers whereby suppliers in Australia and New Zealand would share designs with no licence fee involved.
"That's part of the deal and they can cross pollinate designs as well - everyone is very happy with that," Page said.
Harvey earlier told the meeting the company's sales in the first four months of the 1996/97 year (July-June) rose 11.3 percent to A$361.9 million.
At 3.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), Harvey Norman shares were steady at A$6.25.
